target: route "degenerate" -- Degenerate one-player games: ties as a resource, and a run longer than the Holt-Klee ceiling with one player

findings.result_name: degen:cor-hstar-one (the clause "for m=2,3,4 the value is already attained by a DEGENERATE game")
findings.defect: At m=3 and m=4 the exhibited witnesses are harmonic NORMAL FORMS with non-dyadic entries, not games, and the document nowhere proves that such a normal form is realised by a fair-coin SSG. GAP, exactly: "Every rational substochastic harmonic normal form with a strict t0-leak in every row is the harmonic normal form of some stopping one-player SSG." That statement is part of unverified item (v4); frontier.tex's realisability convention is dyadic only (line 6745 "all dyadic with denominator 16, hence realisable by depth-4 trees of average vertices", and the solo round's pipeline ends in "dyadic rounding", rem:hk-survey). The clause is therefore a proved statement whose witness is not an object of the kind the statement is about; the equality h*_1(m)=h*_HK(m)=1,2,4,6 itself is untouched, because its lower bounds come from the dyadic nondegenerate AP games, which I rebuilt as explicit fair-coin SSGs and verified. m=2 is fine (the staircase is an explicit degenerate game).
findings.evidence: deg_m3_run4.json has q^{x2,1}=26566357/27305639040 and deg_m4_run6.json has q^{x1,1}=362854819/4510476448; I computed the lcm of all denominators: 218445112320 (odd part 213325305 = 3*5*29*653*751) and 144335246336 (odd part 140952389 = 17*47*67*2633). No dyadic realisation exists, and by lem:denominator-sharp any realisation needs at least ceil(log2(213325305)) = 28 average vertices, with no construction given anywhere. The route's t_deg3.py/t_deg6.py only search the normal form (`retune` alters QB and calls OP), never build a game; the JSONs store P,Q only. I did verify, from the normal forms, that both reproduce exactly: m=3 S=[0,1,3,6,5,4,5,2], D=[0,0,0,0,2,0,2,0], run 6->3->5->1->0, flat class {4,6} on the run; m=4 run 0->15->8->13->1->5->4, flat class {10,11} off it. Independently, from EXPLICIT fair-coin games I built from the dyadic AP normal forms (N=109 and N=173, stopping by mycore's trap test), the nondegenerate lower bounds h*_1(3)>=4 and h*_1(4)>=6 hold. Note the integrated frontier.tex cor:hstar-one has already dropped this clause and cites only nondegenerate witnesses.

findings.result_name: degen:prop-nolin (the count "24 acyclic unique sink completions of its partial orientation, 17 of them Holt-Klee")
findings.defect: The counts are correct only under an unstated extra condition -- that the completion's bottom-antipodal walk from sigma_0 = 7 is exactly the run 7,11,13. As literally stated ("completions of its partial orientation") the counts are wrong.
findings.evidence: My enumeration of all 2^7 orientations of the seven flat edges, with S fixed on the non-flat edges: 96 are acyclic unique sink orientations, 74 of them Holt-Klee (and all 32 corner resolutions are AUSO, 28 of them HK). Imposing cube.walk(o,7)==[7,11,13] gives exactly 24 and 17, matching the route; their own t_infeas.py does impose it (`w=ba_walk(s,s0,m); if w!=seq: continue`), the LaTeX does not say so. Non-load-bearing: the sentence only supports "L <= h*_HK(4) still holds here", which is trivial since L=2.

findings.result_name: degen:cor-gate (closing sentence "In particular no amount of chaining raises the run length above m+O(1)")
findings.defect: The sentence over-reads the corollary's own hypotheses. Hypothesis (ii) ("a block's vertices never switch while they are dead") is automatic given the chain structure -- a wholly dead block has both options valued 0 at every vertex, hence tied -- but hypothesis (iii) ("no vertex of B_1,...,B_{r-1} switches after the round at which B_r wakes") is NOT automatic, and it excludes precisely the constructions in which earlier blocks keep moving after the last block wakes. What is proved is conditional on (iii); "no amount of chaining" reads as unconditional.
findings.evidence: The proof uses (iii) twice: to conclude T <= m - m_r (the T first-switch witnesses must lie outside B_r) and to conclude that after round T the run is an all-switches run of the frozen subgame. Nothing in the proof bounds a chain in which B_1 and B_r interleave. The route's own next_steps item 4 concedes the point ("the nondegenerate threshold sequencer ... NOT the zero-tie gate, which degen:cor-gate caps").

findings.result_name: degen:lem-gperturb (last sentence, "Condition (*) is the case pi = 0 of (**)")
findings.defect: Not an equivalence. (**) requires (pi,rho) ADMISSIBLE, so its pi=0 case requires rho_{v,a} >= 0 wherever q^{v,a} = 0, whereas (*) allows an arbitrary linear functional d on R^{2m}. Hence (**)|_{pi=0} implies (*) but not conversely, and the two conditions are incomparable rather than nested -- so rem-star's "the stronger condition (**)" is also imprecise. No downstream damage: each condition separately yields L <= h*_HK(m), and cor-onetie's d = y_{x,a} happens to be admissible.
findings.evidence: Admissibility as defined in the lemma constrains rho on exactly the (v,a) with q^{v,a}=0, of which G_lin has six of eight. The proof's identification only shows <rho,y^{sigma}> - <rho,y^{sigma[v]}> has the sign of -Delta(sigma,v), which is a one-way translation of the *values*, not of the *feasible sets*.

findings.defect: The proof asserts that "for a generic admissible (pi',rho')" the first-order term Delta_{(pi',rho')}(sigma,v) is nonzero at every flat incidence, without checking that Delta(sigma,v) is a nonzero functional on the admissible cone. It is -- but the step is asserted, not proved.
findings.evidence: The coefficient of rho_{v,abar} in Delta(sigma,v) is exactly 1 (abar != sigma(v), so rho_{v,abar} does not enter u_sigma = (I-P_sigma)^{-1}(pi_sigma val_sigma + rho_sigma)), and the direction rho_{v,abar} = +1 is admissible whatever q^{v,abar} is; the admissible cone has nonempty interior, so a generic point avoids the finitely many hyperplanes Delta(sigma,v) = 0. One sentence supplies the missing justification.

findings.defect: "the flat classes are exactly the faces of X(G) on which obj is constant" is false as an equality of sets: every sub-face of a flat class is a face on which obj is constant. The correct statement is "the MAXIMAL faces on which obj is constant", which is what the proof's converse actually gives ("the face lies inside one flat class").
findings.evidence: Immediate; the integrated frontier.tex text already reads "the flat classes are exactly the maximal faces of X(G) on which obj is constant".

findings.result_name: degen:cor-hstar-one, as restated in the route's JSON report ("the height-7 class of prop:auso-census is the only class of the 4-cube that one player cannot reach")
findings.defect: Read as a statement about realising ORIENTATIONS this is false: prop:oneplayer-lp forbids every non-Holt-Klee class for nondegenerate one-player games, and the 4-cube has 143-56 = 87 non-HK classes of height 6 alone (the solo round measured 33 of them all failing). The sentence is true only for run LENGTHS. It does not appear in degen.tex, so it is a summary-only over-statement.
findings.evidence: My census: of the 384 height-6-plus outmaps... precisely, my enumeration gives 54912 acyclic height-6 outmaps of which 21504 are Holt-Klee, so most height-6 orientations are non-HK and hence unrealisable by any nondegenerate one-player game (prop:oneplayer-lp). grep of degen.tex for 'only class'/'cannot reach' returns nothing.

findings.result_name: degen:prop-family (the N and a rows of the table) and degen:prop-nolin ("34 vertices, 28 of them average")
findings.defect: These vertex counts are properties of the route's particular Knuth-Yao DDG realisation of the average part, not of the family or of the normal form; the statement presents them as data of the instance. Not an error, but the reader cannot check them from the statement.
findings.evidence: My own depth-k binary-tree realisation of the same block AP_m4_k0_den1024_s1 gives a = 167 average vertices (N = 2m+165) against their a = m+113 (N = 2m+115); for G_lin I get 32 average vertices (N=38) against their 28 (N=34). The load-bearing rows reproduce exactly: L = s+6 and ties = 4s+C(s,2) at s = 0,4,8 (L = 6,10,14; ties = 0,22,60), stopping by the trap test, from the explicit fair-coin game.

findings.defect: "an all-switches run whose resolution lies in the orbit of s_12" should say "whose resolution WITH CORNERS ON THE RUN": a corner resolution depends on the corner choices off the run, so "the" resolution is not well defined, and the proof only handles the run-corner one. (Also worth recording that the proof's contradiction needs s_eps = s', not merely h*_HK(5) < 12; the route gets this right, and the argument is sound, but the statement does not say which fact is doing the work.)
findings.evidence: I verified s_eps = s' does hold in both the m=4 and m=5 arguments: the single flat edge is oriented by d = y_{x,a} towards sigma_0, which is the corner, and S is constant on the class, so the perturbed orientation agrees with the corner resolution everywhere. frontier.tex's integrated text already reads "whose resolution with corners on the run lies in the orbit of s_12".

verdict:
SOUND. Nothing fatal or major survived; the route's two headline theorems are correct and their computational ingredients reproduce exactly under independent reimplementation.

WHAT I REBUILT AND CONFIRMED (all exact rational arithmetic, code in /tmp/claude-1000/-data-ssg-proof/6e64b33d-520c-4c82-aa1b-ffb69ecfcb61/scratchpad/audit-degenerate-correctness/, written from the STATEMENTS):
(1) The census inputs, from scratch in C (enum4.c, 11 s): 5541744 USOs of the 4-cube, 4792176 acyclic; h*(4)=7 attained by exactly 384 outmaps, which I checked form a single free orbit under the 384 cube automorphisms and contain the route's representative (0,1,3,6,7,4,13,10,14,15,9,12,11,8,5,2); NONE of the 384 is Holt-Klee by my own unit-vertex-capacity max-flow test on all 33 faces of dimension >= 2; 21504 acyclic height-6 orientations are Holt-Klee. So h*_HK(4)=6 < 7 = h*(4), independently.
(2) degen:lem-seven-flat, by my own partition enumerator that does NOT assume the "exactly four disjoint (F1)-edges" shortcut: 768 pairs (s, sigma_0) of walk length 7; exactly 384 admit an (F1)-(F4) partition with a block of dimension >= 1; in every one the partition is unique and is the single edge containing the start. The representative's (F1)-edges are exactly {0,1},{6,14},{7,15},{8,9} and its length-7 starts are 8 and 9, as stated.
(3) degen:prop-five: s_12 is a bijective USO, acyclic, of bottom-antipodal height 12, NOT Holt-Klee; its length-12 starts are 0 and 16; its (F1)-subcubes of dimension >= 1 are exactly the seven listed edges; the unique nontrivial (F1)-(F4) partition is {0,16} at start 0, and start 16 admits none.
(4) degen:thm-no-seven: I reconstructed the proof step by step. (F1)-(F4) are genuinely NECESSARY for a real game's flat partition w.r.t. the run-corner resolution -- (F1) because s'(sigma)=S_A | (sigma xor c_A) with S_A disjoint from D_A, (F2) because c_A=sigma_t, (F3) by lem:flat-class(c), (F4) by lem:face-sink -- and I confirmed this empirically on 768 runs of 48 random degenerate m=4 games built as explicit fair-coin SSGs: 0 violations, and the corner resolution is always an AUSO whose BA walk is the run. The dichotomy (nondegenerate, or the unique single-edge partition) is exhaustive, cor-onetie's d = y_{x,a} does satisfy (*) because the two occupancy vertices have disjoint support on (x,a), and the resulting s_eps equals s', which is non-HK. No asserted-not-proved step of consequence.
(5) degen:prop-nolin, twice over: from the normal form AND from an explicit fair-coin SSG I constructed myself (N=38, 32 average, stopping by mycore's trap test). S=(9,10,9,8,9,12,9,12,5,4,7,6,1,0,1,0), D=(6,0,6,0,6,2,6,2,0,0,0,0,2,2,2,2), run 7->11->13, two flat incidences both at x_2 with opposite actions, and y^15-y^13 = (61360/43111)(y^7-y^5) exactly, so (*) is infeasible by Gordan. I also verified the objective identity obj(y^sigma) = sum_v val_sigma(v) on all 16 strategies.
(6) (**) feasibility on that instance, by an explicit admissible certificate of my own: pi^{x2,0}_{x2} + (1/4) pi^{x2,1}_{x1} gives Delta(7,x_2) = -1/40 and Delta(13,x_2) = -2621/18152, both negative; the first direction is free (p=5/16>0), the second sign-constrained and used with the + sign. I also re-derived Delta as the exact epsilon-derivative of the gap, and confirmed u_sigma = (I-P_sigma)^{-1}(pi_sigma val_sigma + rho_sigma).
(7) degen:thm-timer: the proof is correct as written (the three steps -- v is Max and in S_{s-1}; the switch is its first, since an earlier switch would give val_{sigma_{t+1}}(v) > 0 and val is nondecreasing; w' dead at sigma_{s-2}, else v is already switchable there -- all check out, and lem:trap gives "dead = t1 unreachable in G_sigma" for Vmin empty). Empirically: 0 violations of T <= m or of the distinct-first-switch structure over ~18000 wake-up events in 160 tie-rich games at m=4,5, computed from the game; maxT = m exactly at m=4.
(8) degen:prop-staircase, from the game at k = 1,2,4,8,16,24 in both variants: N=k+2, a=0 (resp. a=k), run length exactly k switching {x_1},...,{x_k} in order, T(x_k)=k, val_end = 1 (resp. 2^{-k}), ties on the run = C(k,2).
(9) degen:prop-family rebuilt independently at three sizes s = 0,4,8 from the explicit fair-coin game: L = 6,10,14 = s+6 and ties = 0,22,60 = 4s+C(s,2), stopping, one-player. The switched sets show the staircase running singleton switches for s rounds and then the block reproducing B's own run 0->15->8->13->1->5->4.
(10) degen:prop-partial-lp: the three-case sign law and "flat classes = level sets of sigma -> val_sigma = subcubes" hold with 0 violations over all 2^m strategies of 120 tie-rich m=4 games and 40 m=5 games, all computed from the explicit game. degen:prop-res-nonhk reproduces qualitatively: 800 of 3150 corner resolutions in my sample fail Holt-Klee, at heights 2 and 3.

STANDING-ERROR SWEEP: no greedy policy iteration anywhere (val_sigma is a linear solve restricted to the t1-reaching set, or brute force); rows accumulated rather than dict-literal; sinks carried as sentinels and mapped last; stopping tested by the trap characterisation; run length counts switches, with the non-productive terminal round excluded; the family varies its parameter s; no class-separation via unreachable vertices; no pair test / own-successor issue and no Z_0/Z_1 seed needed, since the route makes no stall claim. The route claims no decision rule, no barrier and no polynomial algorithm, and no step assumes a target-equivalent oracle; the only imported input is Holt-Klee (Holt-Klee, Gaertner-Morris-Ruest), which the route flags as from memory, as rem:oneplayer-lp already does.

CITATIONS CHECKED AGAINST THE TEXT: lem:switch, lem:trichotomy(b),(c), lem:flat-class(a),(b),(c), lem:face-sink, thm:flat-resolution, cor:ceiling-general, lem:trap, lem:trapchar, def:subcube, lem:subgame(b), thm:impedance, prop:oneplayer-lp, prop:auso-census, prop:hstar-five -- all say what the route uses them for. In particular prop:oneplayer-lp's proof does use nondegeneracy only in its final paragraph, so degen:prop-partial-lp(a) is legitimate.

RESIDUAL: the route's declared GAP (whether every one-player run obeys L <= h*_HK(m)) is honestly stated and I found no reason to doubt it is still open. Note that frontier.tex has moved on since this route was written: sec:ties is already integrated (commit 9fafa72) with several of the findings above independently repaired by the integrator -- "maximal faces", the run-corner qualifier in the m=5 statement, the explicit hedge about resolutions in thm:no-seven, and cor:hstar-one's lower bounds now cited from nondegenerate games only -- and h*_HK(5)=11 is now proved (prop:hkfive) rather than measured, which supersedes part of degen:rem-five.
